title: Pharmacological targeting of nuclear factor (erythroid-derived 2)-like 2 (NRF2): a potential strategy to improve the efficacy of oncological photodynamic therapy.
authors: de Klerk, Daniel J; de Keijzer, Mark J; Franchi, Leonardo P; Tian, Jiahao; Gureev, Maxim A; Ge, Yingnan; Mesquita, Barbara; Saelman, Gideon E; Van Herteryck, Isis; Dias, Lionel M; de Haan, Lianne R; Li, Mingjuan; Boyd, Lenka N C; Le Large, Tessa Y S; Giovannetti, Elisa; Kazemier, Geert; Moerland, Perry D; Li, Yunlei; Stubbs, Andrew P; Devreese, Mathias; Porozov, Yuri B; Verheij, Joanne; Lammers, Twan; Khaled, Yazan S; Baron, Byron; Wu, Lingfeng; Heger, Michal
one_liner_zh: 综述NRF2通路抑制剂增强肿瘤光动力疗法疗效，含KEAP1分子对接分析，但核心是药物靶向而非TF-DNA互作建模，仅部分涉及蛋白-蛋白对接，与课题关联较弱。
abstract: The recalcitrance of tumors to photodynamic therapy (PDT) has been linked to PDT-induced activation of survival pathways in sublethally afflicted cancer cells that modulate cellular responses to oxidative stress and damage. Survival signaling manifests in regions of the tumor where the tumor cells are insufficiently photosensitized or subjected to inadequate fluence rates. The survival signaling in these tumor regions is believed to account for tumor recurrence. Accordingly, PDT efficacy can be improved by intervening in these pathways using molecular inhibitors of key modulators of survival signaling, thereby increasing the number of lethally afflicted cancer cells and with it therapeutic efficacy. A promising target for pharmacological intervention is the nuclear factor (erythroid-derived 2)-like 2 (NRF2) pathway, which induces the antioxidant and xenobiotic stress response that helps cells cope with prolonged periods of hyperoxidative stress after PDT. This review outlines our current understanding of this pathway, how it is activated, and how it confers cytoprotective effects and ensures cell survival. Additional distinguishing features of the review are that (1) studies are addressed in which PDT activation of the NRF2 pathway has been demonstrated; (2) a non-exhaustive overview of NRF2 pathway inhibitors is presented that could serve as potential adjuvants in PDT regimens to augment therapeutic efficacy in treatment-resistant tumors and cancers that recur after PDT; (3) molecular docking analyses are included that show potential interactions between the NRF2 inhibitors and the redox sensor KEAP1; and (4) an elaborate account is provided of the potential bottlenecks and caveats that can be encountered when using NRF2 inhibitors in the development of fourth-generation photosensitizers for oncological PDT.
abstract_zh: 肿瘤对光动力疗法（PDT）的顽固性已被关联到PDT诱导的亚致死受损癌细胞中生存通路的激活，这些通路调节细胞对氧化应激和损伤的反应。生存信号在肿瘤中光敏化不足或受到不充分辐照通量率的区域显现。这些肿瘤区域中的生存信号被认为解释了肿瘤复发的原因。因此，通过使用针对生存信号关键调节因子的分子抑制剂干预这些通路，可以增加致死受损癌细胞的数量并随之提高治疗效果，从而改善PDT疗效。一个有前景的药理学干预靶点是核因子（红细胞衍生2）样2（NRF2）通路，该通路诱导抗氧化和外源物应激反应，帮助细胞在PDT后应对长时间的高氧化应激状态。本综述概述了我们目前对该通路的理解、其激活方式以及其如何赋予细胞保护效应并确保细胞存活。综述的其他显著特点包括：（1）讨论了已证明PDT激活NRF2通路的研究；（2）提供了NRF2通路抑制剂的非详尽概述，这些抑制剂可作为PDT方案中的潜在辅助剂，以增强对治疗耐药肿瘤和PDT后复发癌症的治疗效果；（3）包含了分子对接分析，展示NRF2抑制剂与氧化还原传感器KEAP1之间的潜在相互作用；（4）详细阐述了在开发用于肿瘤学PDT的第四代光敏剂时使用NRF2抑制剂可能遇到的潜在瓶颈和注意事项。
